one_line.text: British adman turned behavioural-science consultant who made applied bias research the advertising industry's fashionable toolkit — by actually testing it.

biography.text: Shotton spent two decades in London media agencies before founding Astroten, a consultancy applying behavioural science to marketing for clients including Google, Facebook, and Sky. The Choice Factory (2018) became a #1 Amazon bestseller with over 100,000 copies in 15 languages and won the Business Book Awards' sales-and-marketing category; The Illusion of Choice followed in 2023. He holds an honorary lifetime fellowship of the IPA — the UK advertising industry's professional body — and an associate position at Cambridge's Møller Institute.

background.text: His signature method is the cheap field replication: take a classic laboratory bias, rerun it as a quick real-world test on consumers, and report whether it survives contact with a shopping public — a practitioner's answer to the question academics settle with meta-analyses.

expertise.text: Applied consumer behaviour and advertising effectiveness, credentialed by industry practice and honours rather than academic appointment; his authority is the tested campaign, not the journal.

perspective_and_limits.text: Shotton writes as the evidence wing of an industry he loves, which aims his sharpest fire at advertising's own fads. The limits are structural: a consultant popularising the biases he sells has an interest in their reputation, his quick field tests trade rigour for relevance, and the classic-bias corpus he draws on includes members the replication era has weakened.
